'''Dennis William Hess''' (born March 1, 1947) is an American chemical engineer and academic who is Emeritus Professor of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at the Georgia Institute of Technology.<ref name="AIChEbio" /> His research has focused on thin films, surfaces and interfaces, and plasma processing, including applications in microelectronics manufacturing and materials processing.<ref name="AIChEbio" /> He served as President of The Electrochemical Society (ECS) for the 1996–1997 term and held editor-in-chief roles for ECS journals, including ''Electrochemical and Solid-State Letters'' and the ''ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology''.<ref name="ECSbio" /><ref name="AIChEbio" /><ref name="ECSInterface2003">{{Cite magazine|title=Dennis W. Hess Named Editor for Electrochemical and Solid-State Letters|magazine=The Electrochemical Society Interface|date=Winter 2003|url=https://www.electrochem.org/dl/interface/wtr/wtr03/IF12-03-Pages18-20.pdf|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Hess was born in Reading, Pennsylvania.<ref name="ECSbio" /> He earned a B.S. in chemistry from Albright College and M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in physical chemistry from Lehigh University.<ref name="ECSbio" />

== Career ==
After completing graduate studies, Hess joined Fairchild Semiconductor in Palo Alto, California (1973–1977), where his work included research on silicon oxidation and passivation of semiconductor and dielectric surfaces and interfaces, and later supervision of CMOS process development.<ref name="ECSbio" /><ref name="AIChEbio" />

In 1977, he joined the [[University of California, Berkeley]], as a faculty member in chemical engineering, later serving in administrative roles including Assistant Dean in the College of Chemistry and Vice Chair of the department.<ref name="ECSbio" /><ref name="AIChEbio" /><ref name="BerkeleyTimeline">{{Cite web|title=About the Department of Chemical & Biomolecular Engineering|url=https://chemistry.berkeley.edu/about-dept-cbe|website=University of California, Berkeley College of Chemistry|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref> In 1991, he moved to Lehigh University, where he served as department chair.<ref name="AIChEbio" /><ref name="ECSbio" />

Hess joined the Georgia Institute of Technology faculty in 1996 and served on the faculty through 2020, later becoming emeritus.<ref name="AIChEbio" />

== Research ==
Hess’s research interests include thin films, surfaces and interfaces, and plasma processing, with applications in microelectronics-related materials and device processing.<ref name="AIChEbio" />

== Professional service ==
Hess served as President of The Electrochemical Society for the 1996–1997 term.<ref name="ECSbio" /> He has held editorial leadership roles, including editor-in-chief positions for ECS journals.<ref name="AIChEbio" /><ref name="ECSInterface2003" />

== Awards and honors ==
Hess has received multiple honors from The Electrochemical Society, including:

Honorary Membership (2016).<ref name="ECSHonorary">{{Cite web|title=Honorary Membership|url=https://www.electrochem.org/honorary-membership|website=The Electrochemical Society|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

Edward Goodrich Acheson Award (2012).<ref name="Acheson">{{Cite web|title=Edward Goodrich Acheson Award|url=https://www.electrochem.org/acheson-award|website=The Electrochemical Society|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

Henry B. Linford Award for Distinguished Teaching (2014).<ref name="Linford">{{Cite web|title=Henry B. Linford Award for Distinguished Teaching|url=https://www.electrochem.org/linford-award|website=The Electrochemical Society|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

Gordon E. Moore Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Solid State Science and Technology (2005).<ref name="MooreMedal">{{Cite web|title=Gordon E. Moore Medal for Outstanding Achievement in Solid State Science and Technology|url=https://www.electrochem.org/moore-medal|website=The Electrochemical Society|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

Thomas D. Callinan Award (1993).<ref name="Callinan">{{Cite web|title=Thomas D. Callinan Award|url=https://www.electrochem.org/callinan-award|website=The Electrochemical Society|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

He was named an ACS Fellow in the 2013 class of ACS Fellows.<ref name="ACSFellow2013">{{Cite web|title=2013 ACS Fellows|url=https://cen.acs.org/content/dam/cen/91/30/09130-acsfellows.pdf|website=Chemical & Engineering News (American Chemical Society)|date=2013|access-date=December 28, 2025}}</ref>

Hess has been elected a fellow of multiple professional societies:
* Fellow of The Electrochemical Society (1993).<ref name="ECSQC2005">{{Cite web
 |title=Québec City, Canada - May 15-20, 2005 (General Information and Program)
 |url=https://www.electrochem.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/QC_Prog_Gnrl_Info.pdf
 |website=The Electrochemical Society
 |date=2005
 |access-date=30 December 2025
}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] (1998).<ref name="ECSInterface2003" /><ref name="ECSQC2005" />
* Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (2002).<ref name="ECSInterface2003" /><ref name="ECSQC2005" />
